title: Electronic Components
summary: Fixed and variable resistors and the colour code, resistors in series and parallel, LDRs and thermistors, diodes and LEDs, capacitors and transistors.

notes.text: A **resistor** limits (reduces) the current in a circuit. Its resistance is measured in **ohms (Ω)**; 1 kΩ = 1 000 Ω.
On a four-band resistor: **band 1** = first digit, **band 2** = second digit, **band 3** = multiplier (number of zeros), **band 4** = tolerance (gold ±5%, silver ±10%).

notes.title: Reading a resistor
notes.problem: A resistor has bands yellow, violet, red, gold. What is its value?

notes.label: Memory aid
notes.text: **B**etter **B**e **R**ight **O**r **Y**our **G**reat **B**ig **V**enture **G**oes **W**rong: black, brown, red, orange, yellow, green, blue, violet, grey, white (0 to 9).

notes.caption: The total resistance in parallel is always less than the smallest resistor

notes.title: Combining resistors
notes.problem: Two 100 Ω resistors are connected (a) in series and (b) in parallel. Find the total resistance.

rows: Resistance changed by turning a knob or sliding
Resistance **decreases** as light increases (high resistance in the dark)
Allows current to flow in **one direction only**; protects circuits and converts AC to DC
A diode that gives off light; uses little energy and lasts long; needs a series resistor
Stores electrical charge and releases it; used for timing circuits and smoothing current; measured in farads (µF)
An electronic switch or amplifier with three legs (**collector, base, emitter**). A small current into the base switches on a larger current from collector to emitter

notes.label: Remember
notes.text: The LED's longer leg is the **anode** (+) and the shorter leg, next to the flat edge, is the **cathode** (−).
